skills.title: Name cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere
Match everyday objects to their 3D shape
Recognise a 3D shape in any position or size
Say what a solid looks like from the top, front and side
Match a top, front or side view to the object
Explain why the same object looks different from different places

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a person sitting in another place sees the same view they see
signs: Says a friend opposite sees the same side
Cannot say what is hidden from the other person
Gives their own view for someone else's

misconceptions.belief: Draws what they know is on the object, not what can be seen from that place
signs: Draws a hidden cup handle
Draws three faces of a cube in the front view
Says 'but it has a handle' when the handle is behind

skills.title: Copy a shape on a dot or square grid by counting units along each side
Recognise that a shape turned or moved on a grid is still the same shape and size
Make and continue tile patterns on a grid

misconceptions.belief: Counts dots instead of the gaps between them when measuring a line on a dot grid
signs: Says a line touching 4 dots is 4 units long
Copied shapes come out one unit too long
Points at dots while counting instead of at spaces

skills.title: Convert distances to the same unit before comparing
Order three or more distances given in mixed units
Find how much farther one distance is than another

misconceptions.belief: Compares numbers without matching the units, so 2 km < 500 m
signs: Says 900 m is longer than 1 km
Looks only at the numbers
Orders mixed distances by digit count

skills.title: Show that adding consecutive odd numbers from 1 gives square numbers
Show that two consecutive triangular numbers add to a square number
Test a pattern on new cases and explain with a picture why it always works

misconceptions.belief: Thinks any run of odd numbers adds to a square, even if it does not start at 1 or skips one
signs: Claims 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 is a square
Adds 1 + 3 + 7 and expects a square
Does not notice the missing L-shapes

misconceptions.belief: Thinks adding odd numbers always gives an odd number
signs: Expects 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 to be odd
Rejects 16 as an answer because 'odd + odd should be odd'
Says 3 + 5 is odd

skills.title: Decide whether a situation needs an exact or an approximate value
Round large numbers to a sensible place (thousand, lakh, crore)
Judge how big the error from rounding is
Write repeated multiplication in exponential form and name base and exponent
Evaluate powers, including powers of negative numbers
Compare how fast powers grow against repeated addition

misconceptions.belief: Thinks base and exponent can be swapped (2⁵ = 5²)
signs: Says 2⁵ and 5² are equal
Writes 4³ as 3 × 3 × 3 × 3
Does not notice which number is small and raised

skills.title: Name the parts of a circle: radius, chord, diameter, arc, segment, sector
Relate diameter, radius and chords
Describe a circle's reflection and rotation symmetries

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a circle has only 2 or 4 lines of symmetry
signs: Draws just a vertical and a horizontal line
Says "4, like a square"
Does not realise any diameter works

misconceptions.belief: Confuses a sector with a segment
signs: Calls a pizza slice a segment
Calls the piece cut off by a straight cut a sector
Uses the words interchangeably

skills.title: Predicts that things with a curved surface roll
Predicts that things with flat faces slide
Predicts that things with flat tops and bottoms stack
Knows the same thing can roll one way and stand or stack another way

misconceptions.belief: Believes only balls can roll
signs: Says a bottle or a tin cannot roll
Names only balls when asked what rolls
